source.stem: By which process does oxygen pass out of a leaf?

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: A living seed will germinate even when conditions are unsuitable.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A wooden pencil is living because it came from a plant that grew from a seed.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: A dry, ungerminated seed is non-living.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: The young plant is the seed's offspring.

intelligence.enrichment: A seed is connected to living processes because, under suitable conditions, it germinates into a young plant that grows and can later be part of a life cycle producing new seeds. Favourable conditions allow the seed to show growth as a plant; the observed germination supports placing the seed with living things. The learner correctly applies this rule: A seed is connected to living processes because, under suitable conditions, it germinates into a young plant that grows and can later be part of a life cycle producing new seeds. A seed is just a small non-living object until it visibly sprouts.
